Marissa — thanks for putting this together. Quick legal summary from my side: 

- Controls: Ironclad's in-workflow redlines and audit trail are very convenient, but DocuSign has stronger provenance metadata for global legal acceptance in certain jurisdictions (notably EU eIDAS and APAC use cases).
- Evidence retention: we need guaranteed WORM storage for signed artifacts; currently both vendors offer this as add-ons — check the SLA differences (RPO/RTO).
- Keys: If we centralize KMS or HSM, we need an integration plan so private keys remain customer-controlled; Ironclad supports bring-your-own-key for enterprise plans, DocuSign supports HSM at higher tiers.
- Migration: preserving the chain of custody for previously signed docs will require a verification mapping to the new provider's audit schema (likely non-trivial).

Major blocker is any feature that would degrade our ability to certify historic signatures during audits. If procurement can find parity on retention/KMS terms, consolidation is viable.

-Markus

Hi Marissa / Markus / Laura — thanks for including Ironclad in this conversation. A few points from our side that may help the decision: 

1) Pricing: I've attached a short two-page PDF that shows enterprise consolidation pricing as well as typical migration credits we offer to offset retained DocuSign agreements. The big levers are per-seat enterprise tiers + transaction buckets; we've seen customers reduce total per-unit cost by 18–30% after consolidation.

2) Migration: we provide a migration toolkit and partner services (we can also introduce our migration partner). The toolkit preserves signature metadata and includes a validation report for the first 10k documents. For anything beyond that we do a phased migration to preserve auditability.

3) Compliance: Ironclad supports SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, and offers eIDAS-compatible signature flows with add-on modules. For KMS, we support AWS KMS + external HSM integrations on our enterprise plan; scope and pricing depend on whether you want Redwood keys or customer-managed keys.
